answer: Each agent enrolls inside a hardware enclave and every submission carries a fresh nonce signed there, so a copied answer arrives with a nonce that does not match the measured machine, and the mismatch shows up as a second echo of the same device. Because the attestation is burned as soon as a recruit is caught, a farm must buy a new enclave per identity per cycle, which turns every fake into a hardware bill instead of a cheap whisper, and the lantern of shared hardware goes out at the first audit.
